Food for thought

This move was likely at/near its top regardless-- the normal signs started to flash with the leaders rolling over, alt OI and volume dominance-- but we added a "new" FUD which accelerated into a forceful move down

It isn't really new, we knew to be aware of this back before Mythos/Fable class model. What we didn't know is how long it would take to materialize as fear in market participants holding a significant percent of their portfolios onchain/in cryptoassets. Fair to say there's a fatter left tail and more of a chance of it materializing sooner than we thought. 

People instinctively want to label the market as a "bull" or "bear" but it's long been a dispersion market regardless. Even if we are in a "bull" for real money-generating protocols, there's going to be some dead periods and wild 2way vol. I'm going to continue to focus on medium/higher timeframe swings where many liquid 2-6x's have been available with an overall lower % of portfolio. 

Hard to overstate how much better you can sleep with the safety/security of TradFi for the vast majority of portfolio.

Smart contracts have been live on Ethereum for 11 years.

& on their own, they still can't read a webpage.

Everything they know has to be fed to them as a clean number. Prices. Timestamps. Balances.

The real world is messier. News articles, PDFs, agreements written in English, two sources that disagree.

That's the gap @GenLayer built Intelligent Contracts for.

𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨

• fetch & read live web pages
• process text, PDFs & images
• follow rules written in plain English
• use AI to judge outcomes that aren't a simple yes or no
• settle the result on-chain

𝐡𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐲 𝐡𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐭

• 5 random validators check each result
• each one runs a different model or config
• majority rules
• appeal it & the panel jumps to 11, then 23, then 47

Anthropic counts revenue generated through cloud partners such as AWS and Google Cloud, while OpenAI apparently does not. Investors had therefore adjusted OpenAI’s reported figures to make them comparable with Anthropic’s, which helped produce the ~$70B estimate.

So we are essentially talking about whether revenue flowing through cloud partners is included in the headline number or not.

That is a comparability issue, not some sudden collapse in OpenAI’s revenue trajectory.

The fact that the market is treating this as a major negative for AI is, frankly, pretty ridiculous.
